our_argument_summary: We verdict WIN-005 as 'Std Model Explains': MHD reversed-flux patch dynamics at the core-mantle boundary reproduce the observed SAA inter-cell decay asymmetry from first principles. The dome has no fluid core, no MHD equations, and no mechanism to produce asymmetric decay rates between separate SAA cells; its 'aetheric field geometry' invocation is non-falsifiable. The claim also fails the post-hoc test (CHAOS-7 / INTERMAGNET / IGRF data publicly available at write-time).

The 'source' field credits 'INTERMAGNET TTB annual means (WIN-015)', NOT WIN-005. The text string 'African' / '23,050' / '21,880' / 'WIN-005' / 'WIN_005' / 'cell' appears NOWHERE in monitor.py. WIN-005 lives purely in inject_ai_layer.py as a static metadata row: { id: 'WIN-005', title: 'African cell decays faster', data_source: 'CHAOS-7', year: 2025, observed: '23,050 to 21,880 nT', status: 'confirmed' }. No code reads CHAOS-7 to verify these observed values, and no per-cell decay rate is computed anywhere.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Standard MHD (Terra-Nova et al. 2017, DOI 10.1016/j.pepi.2017.03.002 — title 'Relating the South Atlantic Anomaly and geomagnetic flux patches'; CHAOS-7 model Finlay et al. 2020 DOI 10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9 — title 'The CHAOS-7 geomagnetic field model and observed changes in the South Atlantic Anomaly') explains SAA inter-cell asymmetry from reversed-flux patches in the outer-core fluid. The dome 'predicts' the same asymmetry via 'aetheric field geometry' with no specified equations. Both DOIs verified to resolve and to be on-topic.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: CHAOS-7 (Finlay et al. 2020, formally published 2020 in Earth, Planets and Space) and INTERMAGNET / IGRF cell decay data were in the public scientific literature years before WIN-005 was created in the dome's monitor (inject_ai_layer.py git history would be needed to date the literal; the wins.json field 'new_in_v51' is False, suggesting WIN-005 has been in the model for multiple major versions). The dome adopts the published asymmetric-decay observation and labels it 'confirmed'.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The dome cites no equation that takes disc_radius=20015 km / firmament_height=9086 km / sun_altitude=5733 km / moon_altitude=2534 km as inputs and produces 23,050 nT or 21,880 nT or any decay rate as output. The only numerical content is the observed value adopted verbatim from CHAOS-7. The 'aetheric field geometry predicts' phrasing is asserted, never derived.

holes_found.description: Numerical inconsistency between WIN-005 and WIN-035, both about the same SAA African cell using the same CHAOS-7 data source. WIN-005's detail_evidence states CHAOS-7 quantifies cell decay rates as 'roughly 160–200 nT/year' (Brazilian/Atlantic) and 'roughly 80–120 nT/year' (East Indian Ocean). WIN-035's detail_evidence states the SAA African cell decays at '~28–30 nT/yr for decades'. The dome's own raw data (23,050→21,880 nT over 2000–2025) implies ~47 nT/yr, intermediate between but consistent with neither set of numbers we quote. A dome defender reading both pages will ask: 'which is it — 28-30, 47, 80-120, or 160-200 nT/yr?' Internal-consistency is the first methodological principle of the review; we should not present three different decay-rate magnitudes across cross-referenced WINs without disambiguating that they refer to (presumably) different geographic targets or measurement metrics (point-minimum rate vs cell-centroid average vs INTERMAGNET single-station rate vs CHAOS-7 spherical-harmonic fit at extremum). The numbers may all be correct, but the WIN-005 detail_evidence makes no attempt to specify what metric '160-200 nT/year' represents, why it differs from WIN-035's '28-30 nT/yr', or how it relates to the dome's adopted 23050/21880 pair.
holes_found.recommendation: Patch WIN-005 detail_evidence to (a) state explicitly what metric the 160-200 / 80-120 nT/yr figures represent (CHAOS-7 spherical-harmonic field at the local minimum vs station-level annual mean vs cell-area-integrated rate), (b) reconcile with WIN-035's 28-30 nT/yr TTB station figure, and (c) tie back to the dome's adopted 23050→21880 nT pair so a cross-referencing reader sees one coherent picture. Alternatively, drop the specific 160-200/80-120 numbers and use only the qualitative 'factor-of-two differential' which WIN-035's TTB number can also support.

holes_found.description: Geographic-naming ambiguity. WIN-005's claim title is 'African SAA cell faster decay' (and the dome's claim per inject_ai_layer.py is 'African cell decays faster'). Our detail_evidence then quantifies asymmetry in terms of 'South Atlantic (Brazilian) cell' vs 'East Indian Ocean cell' — neither of which is unambiguously the 'African' cell. Depending on which literature convention the reader brings, 'African' could mean either lobe (the eastward-emerging secondary lobe under southern Africa / Indian Ocean, OR the primary lobe under the South Atlantic which physically lies west of the African continent). The result is that our text quantifies a differential between two cells we name differently from the dome and from our own claim title; a reader can plausibly read our evidence as saying the SLOWER cell (East Indian Ocean, 80-120) is what the dome calls 'African', which would directly contradict the dome's 'African = faster' claim and our own kernel-of-truth concession.
holes_found.recommendation: Standardise on one geographic naming scheme and apply it across WIN-004, WIN-005, WIN-035. Most cleanly: rename the dome's 'African cell' to 'the eastern (African/Indian Ocean) lobe' on first mention in detail_evidence, then use a single label throughout. State once which lobe the dome predicts to decay faster and which CHAOS-7 number matches it.

holes_found.description: monitoring='hardcoded' tag is defensible but obscures a sharper point. The dome's monitor.py has ZERO logic that touches WIN-005 — no domain, no fetch, no comparator. WIN-005 lives only as a static metadata row in inject_ai_layer.py. The literal '23,050 to 21,880 nT' string is hardcoded, so 'hardcoded' is not wrong, but the more interesting structural fact is that WIN-005 is unmonitored: it is asserted-confirmed in metadata, not tested by code. This is a meaningful distinction for Part 2b counts ('hardcoded' implies a comparison that always passes by construction; 'metadata-only' implies no comparison at all). The current binary tag schema cannot express this distinction, but the detail_evidence could.
holes_found.recommendation: Add one sentence to detail_evidence noting that the dome's monitor.py has no domain for WIN-005 — the 'confirmed' status is asserted in inject_ai_layer.py metadata, not produced by any code comparison. This sharpens the post-hoc argument: not only was the observed value publicly available at write-time, the dome doesn't even pretend to verify it programmatically.

stronger_arguments.description: Strengthen by using the dome's own numbers. The dome asserts African cell 23,050→21,880 nT over 2000-2025 (=46.8 nT/yr); this is internally consistent with WIN-035's 28-30 nT/yr TTB station figure to within ordinary geographic/instrument variation. By contrast, the dome offers NO quantitative prediction for the West (Brazilian/Atlantic) cell decay rate — the 'asymmetry' is purely qualitative on the dome's side. Standard MHD via CHAOS-7 spherical harmonics produces specific decay rates per location that match observation to ~5%. Our 'Std Model Explains' verdict is much stronger when framed as 'standard model produces quantitative per-location decay rates; dome produces only a one-word qualitative claim'.

Strengthen by noting the dome's nomenclature inheritance. The dome calls its cells 'African' and 'American' — exactly the same labels used in modern CHAOS-7 / IGRF literature. The dome has not coined new terminology that would be needed if it were modelling from first principles on a flat disc with a single aetheric pole. The naming itself is a tell that the dome adopted the standard-model geographic decomposition wholesale, including the differential decay finding.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome correctly observes that the SAA has an asymmetric inter-cell decay structure and correctly adopts the published CHAOS-7 values (wins.json WIN-005 detail_evidence cites '23,050 to 21,880 nT' for the African cell — these specific numbers are independently checkable against CHAOS-7 model output). The recognition that two SAA cells exist and decay at different rates is itself a non-trivial observation and the dome accurately reflects it. This is more than nothing.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Per WIN-005 detail_evidence, the dome 'predicts' the asymmetry via 'aetheric field geometry' with no equations, no predicted decay rates, no specification of which cell should be faster, and no derivation from disc_radius / firmament_height. Per the live monitor.py inspection (no WIN-005 domain present), the 'confirmation' is metadata assertion in inject_ai_layer.py:49 not a code-checked numerical comparison. Per WIN-035's detail_evidence the same data was in WMM/IGRF for years before PROS-005 was registered 2026-03-06, failing the Part 3.1b post-hoc carve-out (data 'not plausibly known to the author at write-time'). Recognising a published observation and asserting an unspecified mechanism explains it is not the same as predicting the observation.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A capable dome defender would argue: 'You concede the African cell decays faster (kernel of truth). You concede the dome has identified two cells with differential decay. You concede the dome's adopted numerical values match CHAOS-7. The dome model therefore makes a falsifiable prediction (African > American in decay rate) that has been confirmed. That this prediction can also be produced by MHD is irrelevant under our review's own principle (Part 1, internal-consistency-first) that a model is judged on whether ITS predictions match data, not on whether competitor models also fit. Our review converts a successful binary qualitative prediction (which cell decays faster) into a failure by demanding numerical specificity the dome never claimed — that is goalpost-moving. The proper verdict is therefore something like Std Model Also Explains, not Std Model Explains in a way that downgrades the dome.'
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Add a paragraph to detail_verdict_text addressing this directly: 'The dome's prediction is binary and qualitative (African > American in decay rate). It is falsifiable in that narrow sense — had the American cell decayed faster, the prediction would have failed. We accept this. The Std Model Explains verdict does not deny the prediction; it observes that (i) a binary qualitative prediction with two outcomes provides ~1 bit of information vs. CHAOS-7's per-location rate prediction which constrains continuously, and (ii) the dome registered the prediction after the asymmetry was already public CHAOS-7 output (post-hoc carve-out fails). A model whose only predictions are 1-bit qualitative claims about phenomena already quantified elsewhere is not advancing the science even when its bit is right.' This neutralises the goalpost-moving framing by acknowledging the narrow win and explaining precisely why it does not generalise.

cross_win_consistency.inconsistencies_found: WIN-005 detail_evidence quantifies the SAA inter-cell decay differential as 160-200 nT/yr (Brazilian) vs 80-120 nT/yr (East Indian Ocean). WIN-035 detail_evidence quantifies the SAA African cell decay as ~28-30 nT/yr. WIN-005 says CHAOS-7 is the source; WIN-035 says WMM/IGRF/INTERMAGNET is the source. The dome's own raw value (23050→21880 over 25y = 46.8 nT/yr) sits between these and is consistent with neither set. WIN-004 separately and more carefully notes 'Terra-Nova et al. (2017) does not specifically derive the inter-cell bifurcation rate' — a precise qualifier that WIN-005 omits when it claims Terra-Nova 'demonstrate[s] that reversed-flux patches in the core generate the SAA splitting and differential decay rates matching observations'. WIN-005 slightly overstates Terra-Nova's quantitative reach relative to WIN-004's more conservative framing.

deeper_analysis: The verdict 'Std Model Explains' is correct and survives a third look. The structural argument (no fluid core in the dome ⇒ no MHD ⇒ no mechanism for asymmetric decay rates) is sound; the post-hoc objection (CHAOS-7 data publicly available pre-registration) is sound; both supporting citations now have correct DOIs and verified titles. The weak points in this WIN are not in the verdict, they are in the supporting numerical apparatus: the 160-200 / 80-120 nT/yr cell decay figures appear without an explicit source citation in detail_evidence (we cite 'CHAOS-7 geomagnetic field model' in general, not a specific table or figure), and they are not reconciled with the ~28-30 nT/yr figure used in our own WIN-035. The geographic naming (African vs Atlantic vs Brazilian vs East Indian Ocean) is also handled inconsistently across the WIN-004/005/035 cluster. None of these is verdict-changing, but a careful dome defender would notice and use them. Recommended action is minor_edit (numerical/nomenclature reconciliation across the cluster) plus the advocate-mode preemptive paragraph in detail_verdict_text.

summary_for_decider: Spot-check of WIN-005 (last review 2026-04-06, ~58d stale). Verdict (Std Model Explains) survives — robust structural argument plus verified citations. Three holes found, all moderate or major, all addressable via minor edits to detail_evidence/detail_verdict_text. Highest-priority hole: cross-WIN numerical inconsistency — WIN-005 cites 160-200 vs 80-120 nT/yr, WIN-035 cites 28-30 nT/yr, dome's own data implies 46.8 nT/yr; need to reconcile or drop the specific numbers in WIN-005. Second hole: geographic naming ('African' / 'Atlantic' / 'Brazilian' / 'East Indian Ocean') used inconsistently across the WIN-004/005/035 cluster. Third hole: monitoring=hardcoded tag is defensible but the sharper fact is that WIN-005 has zero presence in monitor.py — purely a metadata row in inject_ai_layer.py, no comparator. Cycle-2 critical fixes (CHAOS-7 DOI, monitoring tag) were both verified APPLIED. Advocate-mode defense rated 3/5: the 'binary qualitative prediction is still a prediction' line is genuine and merits a preemptive paragraph.
